title: Internal JWT claims (C2)
description: Payload of the ES256 JWT issued by the gateway for MCP servers and the credential broker. Rules that a schema cannot express and that receivers MUST check: kid not starting with 'test-' unless the receiver is explicitly configured with allowTestKeys=true (unit tests and dev, CC-044), and kid not starting with 'dev-' unless the receiver is in dev mode, that is the devstack profile and allowTestKeys=true together (CC-137; allowTestKeys alone is not enough for dev-), signature against the gateway JWKS, iss, aud == own id (exception, CC-249: aud `mcp-pending`, the audience of the probe at add time when the serverId is not yet known, is accepted by a server only for use `manifest` on GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest and only while the server holds no policy data, i.e. has never accepted a push; for nothing else), exp with clock skew <= 30 s, iat not more than 30 s in the future, exp - iat <= 60 s, jti not seen within its validity window (one-time, for every purpose), rid == X-Request-Id header, purpose: `use` == the purpose of the endpoint, otherwise the token is refused as wrong_purpose (CC-249): `manifest` only for GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest and `policy-data` only for POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data of a server (C14), both only in the service variant; `call` for everything else (the MCP endpoint of a server, every endpoint of the credential broker) and never for those two paths; tool present and == params.name for tools/call, tool present for the broker resolve and for the authenticator calls of the gateway (GET /v1/authenticator, POST /v1/authenticator/verify, POST /v1/authenticator/invalidate-codes; CC-092, CC-128), tool absent for every other request (CC-038), service variant only for initialize, server/discover, tools/list, ping, GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest, POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data and (broker) GET /v1/systems, and only outside a session (stateless, CC-070): notifications/*, GET/DELETE on the MCP endpoint, subscriptions/listen and every other request of a session carry the user variant without tool. A tools/call retry with inputResponses (MRTR, MCP 2026-07-28) is an ordinary tools/call with a fresh token (CC-069). mcp_risk and mcp_action (CC-226) only when the receiver is the sidecar of an adapter, otherwise invalid_claims. Any failure -> HTTP 401.

Header.description: JOSE header. Receivers accept only ES256 and only a kid present in the gateway JWKS; a kid starting with 'test-' is rejected unless allowTestKeys=true (CC-044); a kid starting with 'dev-' is rejected unless the devstack profile and allowTestKeys=true are both set (CC-137).

aud.description: Id of the receiving component: mcp-<system> or mcp-credential-broker. A single string, never an array. The value mcp-pending is the audience of the manifest token that the gateway sends at add time, before the serverId is known (use manifest, GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest only, and only while the server holds no policy data).

prv.description: Revision of the policy data of the gateway (C7): a server that sees a revision newer than the one it holds refreshes its policy data at once. 0 means a gateway without policy data; receivers must not infer anything about policy from it (CC-068).

use.description: Purpose of the token (CC-249). call: a request of the MCP endpoint of a server or of the credential broker (user variant, or the service variant for initialize, server/discover, tools/list, ping and the broker GET /v1/systems). manifest: the pull of the manifest of a server, GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest (C14). policy-data: the push of policy data to a server, POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data (C14). A receiver refuses a token whose purpose is not the one of the endpoint, whatever else is valid, so that a token minted for one purpose cannot be used for another.

UserClaims.description: Call on behalf of a user. The only variant accepted for tools/call and by the broker resolve and authenticator endpoints.

ServiceClaims.description: Gateway call without a user and without a session. Accepted only for initialize, server/discover, tools/list, ping (use call), GET /.well-known/mcp-manifest (use manifest) and POST /.well-known/mcp-policy-data (use policy-data) of a server, and GET /v1/systems of the broker (use call) (CC-069, CC-070, CC-249).

sub.description: sub from the IdP token (C1), unchanged.

grp.description: User groups from C9, only those with the mcp- prefix.

azp.description: OAuth client id of the AI client (C1).

tool.description: Server-side name of the tool being called. Present exactly for tools/call (and for the broker resolve and authenticator calls that serve it); absent for initialize, server/discover, subscriptions/listen, tools/list, and ping (CC-038, CC-069).

mfa.description: Seconds since the last authentication at an MFA acr level. Absent means unknown.

use.description: The user variant is only ever for calls (CC-249).

UserBase.description: Claims shared by the user variant for every receiver (CC-038, CC-069).

AdapterUserClaims.description: User variant for a receiver that is the sidecar of an adapter (CC-226, CC-193): the claims of UserClaims plus the classification of the administrator from the registry, as mcp_risk and mcp_action. Both come together, only with tool (a tools/call), and must fit each other (read for READ_ONLY, update or admin for UPDATE, delete or admin for DESTRUCTIVE). The gateway sends them only to a server that its configuration puts in adapter mode; the schema cannot tell the receiver, so the rule of the receiver is normative: a receiver that is not the sidecar of an adapter (a native server, the credential broker) rejects a token that carries mcp_risk or mcp_action as invalid_claims. The names are not act (RFC 8693, actor) on purpose.
